subject: Private deployment: hardware details & offline ops follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rodriguez <maya.rodriguez@biomedica.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: hardware details & offline ops follow-up

Hi Maya — thanks again for the call earlier today. I wanted to capture the key open items on our side so we can move the qualification forward for a private, air-gapped deployment. Quick recap of what we discussed: 

- You're leaning toward an on-prem/private VPC install to control PHI traffic and keep model data in-house.
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization and batch embeddings for search.
- Peak concurrency estimate you shared: ~30 concurrent low-latency requests during business hours; large nightly batch for embeddings.

Open items we need from you to confirm sizing and offline ops: 
1) Hardware inventory: current GPU hosts (model, VRAM), CPU, disk, network topology. If you can fill the attached hw-inventory-template.xlsx that’s ideal.
2) Upgrade window policy: how often do you apply kernel/firmware upgrades that would require us to support an offline upgrade path?
3) Air-gap constraints: are there any policy restrictions on removable media for bringing software/artifacts on-site?
4) Offline monitoring: who will run the local ops playbooks (SRE, infra team), and do you have on-call escalation we should coordinate with?

Next steps I propose:
- You return the hw template and any constraints.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer (Monica) to align on install artifacts and upgrade cadence.

I’ll attach a short draft of our offline-ops checklist so you can see the level of detail we usually require.

Thanks, and happy to hop on a follow-up tomorrow if that helps.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

From: Maya Rodriguez <maya.rodriguez@biomedica.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@biomedica.com
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: hardware details & offline ops follow-up

Aditya — thanks for the summary and the checklist draft, very helpful. I attached a quick pass at the inventory and answered the upgrade questions inline below. High level answers:

- Inventory: See attached hw-inventory-template.xlsx (we filled model names & VRAM). Primary hosts are three NVIDIA A40s (48GB) used for inference, one spare A100 (40GB) for burst testing, and a 16-core CPU headnode.
- Upgrade cadence: Our infra team does quarterly maintenance windows; firmware/kernel upgrades occur during those windows and are scheduled at least 2 weeks in advance.
- Air-gap constraints: We cannot accept external USB drives into the data center without a security sweep; encrypted transfer over a designated jump host is preferred.
- Local ops: We have a small infra team (ops@biomedica.com) that will own day-to-day; I will introduce you to Ravi (ops lead) on the technical call. On-call escalation is handled via PagerDuty and a secondary phone rotation.

Questions from our side:
1) What is Redwood's recommended strategy for applying model updates in an air-gapped environment — do you ship a signed binary bundle we transfer into the network, or do you provide a build script we run locally?
2) For nightly batch embeddings, can we run the job offline and sync embeddings back to your hosted service, or must all embedding compute be local in our model?

I can do a technical deep-dive with Monica on Wednesday morning PT. Please send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Rodriguez
CTO, Biomedica Therapeutics
maya.rodriguez@biomedica.com

Attachment: hw-inventory-template.xlsx (filled)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rodriguez <maya.rodriguez@biomedica.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: hardware details & offline ops follow-up

Thanks Maya — that's exactly what we needed, appreciate the quick turn. Short answers to your questions: 

1) Model updates in air-gapped installs: we provide signed, versioned artifact bundles (tgz) that your infra team imports via the approved transfer method (jump host). The bundle contains a hash and a signature so you can validate integrity without external connectivity. For customers that prefer, we can also provide a reproducible build script and a locked container image you can build locally — both approaches are supported.

2) Nightly batch embeddings: both modes supported. If you want embeddings to remain on-prem, Redwood can run entirely local inference and you push the results into your search index. If you prefer hybrid (local compute + sync), we provide secure rsync templates and an import tool, but note that syncing to our hosted embeddings service requires explicit security review and additional contracts.

Proposed next steps and owners:
- Technical deep-dive (Monica): scope install artifacts, artifact transfer process, and upgrade playbook — scheduled for Wed 2026-07-08 09:30 PT. Monica to lead. (Monica: can you share an agenda and a brief install artifact checklist?)
- I will loop Vivek on sizing recommendations based on the A40/A100 mix and nightly batch volume.
- Post-call: we'll produce a short SOW + deployment runbook for your compliance team.

I'll attach the draft offline ops checklist and a short note describing the signed-bundle workflow.

Best,
Aditya
